newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up, propped by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up, propped by blue chips.

text.p: The Philippine equities market closed up for the fourth straight session as investors ignored the Dow Jones and PLDT's fall and bought index heavyweights, traders said.
"It seems investors were positioning for issues that are worthy of a 25 to 30 percent growth in income or those with good prospects in 1997," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc.

"We are not following the Dow except for major movements. It seems that with the continued gradual rise in shares, we are building a solid base so it looks like we are going to have a good first six months," said Irving Ackerman at brokerage I. Ackerman & Co Inc.
He said that the index may reach 3,400 points by mid-year.
On Wednesday, the Dow dropped by 52 points while PLDT's American Depositary Receipts lost $0.25.
As a result, traders said the market opened down but was brought out of negative territory in early trade by buying on blue chips Petron Corp, PNB and San Miguel.
At the end of trading, gainers beat losers 84 to 56 with 57 issues unchanged. All sectors went up except for the property sector. Value turnover was seen aat an average 2.5 billion pesos.
Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities said although the market seems bullish in the long-term, the index may move within the 3,150 to 3,250 points range on Friday.
